articles.title: A publisher told her a book was “not so much written as it was preached”
articles.deck: Peggy Kennedy was preaching as a teenager and writing nothing. Then, driving to a Saturday luncheon, she heard herself say a sentence about an apple tree that she had not planned to say.

hero.alt: Rev. Peggy I. Kennedy photographed smiling, against a designed background

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the June 2013 issue. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is otherwise the author's. The facing page carried a paid panel advertising the author's three books, labelled ADVERTORIAL in the original. That panel is not reproduced here. This essay carried no such label.

body.v: “If you can ever get under an apple tree with God, do it! There He will awaken you with His love and you will arise to go with Him.”

I marvelled as I heard myself sharing this phrase. The setting was a Saturday morning luncheon where, as the guest speaker, I would be sharing the word of God with the dedicated followers of the Lord. I found myself telling them the conversation I had had with the Lord en route to the meeting.
That conversation was all about writing. I would be writing in not one but three streams — the apple tree would be first.

This announcement from the Lord was but His latest in the sequence of words I was hearing about writing. It was not unusual for people to approach me and say “you should write a book”, or “there's a book in you!” Obviously, with this new round of disclosures I was getting closer to the discovery of a whole new realm of ministry to the Body of Christ.
Preaching first

I began my calling to the pulpit ministry early — in fact I was preaching when I was still a teenager. Convinced of the call of God, I pursued training in Bible school as well as diverse opportunities of ministry. The early arena of ministry was among Canada's first peoples. Also, in luncheons or conferences, I was invited to speak to women who had a desire to press in to receive more from the Lord.
I've known the unique delight of watching the Spirit of the Lord take the word and minister it into the “now” moments of the hearers, whether in Canada or internationally.
I've always been drawn to the narrative portions of the word of God. Those are more than “stories”. They tell of real-life partnerships with a living God.
After many years of ministry I heard about an author who said that her book was “not so much written as it was preached”. That line became embedded in my heart.
body.highlight: not so much written as it was preached

body.v: Three streams

The accumulation of the Lord's details about writing was growing. It was 1999 when He clearly indicated that my first book would be written from my six-month personal daily journal of discoveries I had made in the Song of Songs.

Those journals became A Is for Apple — Daily Delights from the Song of Songs, released in 2009. The launch was a major occasion, highlighting how various creative gifts can flow together to bring ministry to the Body of Christ. An artist's painting was the cover, and inside was a worship CD providing a backdrop for each day's devotional page. That focus on complementary giftings was further expressed by four additional authors writing the daily responsive prayers.

In 2012 two more books were released. Hear the Sound is a compilation of the bi-weekly sends which now go out to over 2,500 readers. That book fulfils what the Lord said about the second stream: the fig tree. The emphasis there is on being connected with our God. Like Nathanael, we can discover this gracious, intimate God who sees me under the fig tree and then calls me to participate with Him in greater things. Being connected with Him is essential to being available to Him.
“Where can I get this book?”

Last to be released is Chosen — Conversations of God with His Mighty Warrior. The setting is, of course, Gideon. Like Gideon we can meet our God under the oak tree. There He will speak to us of our destiny and remove our self-imposed disqualifications.

There is a special link of this book to South Asia. I had met a young seminary graduate in India with whom I had a lively discussion about partnering with our God. I made several references to Gideon. Finally the young man interrupted me: “Where can I get this book?” I replied that I had to return to Canada and write it.

That conversation was always before me as I was writing. It truly is a book not so much written as it was preached — I drew heavily upon my notes used when preaching about Gideon in many diverse settings. The book is dedicated to the Gideons whom the Lord is raising up in this generation. I've met them. They are out there. They will partner with Him, and their obedience will merge with the supernatural activity of God.
Is the assignment finished?

The books are now in their first, second and third printings, and two printings are circulating in South Asia. Reader responses have confirmed that the Lord desired that the matters of His heart released from the pulpit would also be heard through my pen.

Is the writing assignment completed? Likely not. Each of the three streams of which the Lord spoke has now been opened. It is predictable that He's preparing more to be released through my ready pen. The anointing can flow from the pulpit. I can certainly now testify that the anointing can also flow from the pen.

articles.title: He lost his job in April and did not find another until November. That was the point
articles.deck: Becky and Sam Khumanthem never planned to open a school. Seven months of unemployment, and a convention in China, changed what they thought they were for.

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the June 2013 issue. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is otherwise the author's.

body.v: For Becky and Sam Khumanthem, opening a Christian school in Hyderabad was something that was never in the plan. But after living here for over five years, it became clear to them that God had been preparing them to do so. Olive Learning Center was dedicated in 2013.

OLC is a Christian school using the Accelerated Christian Education programme, also known as School of Tomorrow. The academic curriculum is anchored in the word of God; character training is infused at every age level; each student's potential is maximised; and it uses computer technology. It is not simply a curriculum, but a system, with manuals schools follow to make the individual learning most successful.
The school's name was inspired by Psalm 128:3, God's promise to those who fear Him: “…your children will be like olive shoots around your table.”
It is our desire to see our children abundantly blessed, having the energy and promise to become great leaders of their generations.
Japan, and a seed

Becky's association with Accelerated Christian Education dated back to 2004, when she was a university student working part-time at a church school in Japan. Later, in 2006, she attended an A.C.E. professional training in Yokohama. This was where God planted in her heart the seed for a Christian education ministry.

After her university studies she worked for a year in a model school using the programme in Japan. In 2008 she returned to India and married Sam. Since then she has been working as India consultant for A.C.E., assisting schools to start, conducting professional trainings, and making school visits.

Sam Khumanthem was in Mumbai before moving to Hyderabad. He worked at a multinational as a communication specialist. After his marriage to Becky, they both decided to settle in Hyderabad, as they thought it a peaceful city compared to the other Indian metros. He continued to work for firms doing similar roles until April 2012.
Seven months

Even though it had become clear that God was leading them to open a Christian school at some point, nothing really happened until April 2012. Sam lost his job and God shut all doors for him. He did not get another job until November 2012.

It was in those seven months that God spoke to Sam in a profound manner. Life is not about you and what you do for yourself, but about God and what you do for Him. It is not about the place you want to go to and do God's work there, but about where God places you to do His work.

In November 2012 they were invited to attend the China Christian Educators' Convention. What they saw there made them see Christian education in a deeper perspective, and it became clear that it was indeed the will of God for them to start a school.
Sam was due to join a job at a PR firm that month. He decided not to. He made a commitment to be in full-time Christian ministry.

We have been experiencing God's miraculous providence in many ways. Without the fervent prayers and generous gifts of God's people, we would not have come this far. OLC is a God-given vision, and we are confident that He who has begun a good work will carry it on until the day of Jesus Christ (Philippians 1:6).

articles.title: I asked the Dean to let me redo five years of study rather than write the dissertation
articles.deck: George Powell on the year that nearly finished him, what the Dean said in reply, and why leadership is a process rather than a place you arrive at.

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the June 2013 issue. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is otherwise the author's.

body.v: Several years ago I achieved a huge goal I had set for myself: earning a doctorate by the time I was 40. I only missed it by one year — but that one year was a killer, and it was the last step in the process that nearly did me in. Writing my dissertation.

For some people that might not be a big deal, but for me it was a gut-wrenching experience, because I'm not the brainy type. I even suggested to the Dean of Students that he let me go back and repeat the previous five years of study in lieu of the dissertation.
Without a moment's hesitation he responded:
George, it's all about the process.

What he was suggesting was that it was not the dissertation that really mattered, but the process I would go through to complete it. Easy for him to say. So I engaged in the process, and I must say it taught me a lot. It taught me about persistence and discipline, what I was really made of, and about not giving up when everything in me wanted to throw in the towel.
Leadership is the same way

No one ever became a leader in a day, a month, or even years. Why? Because leadership isn't about a destination — it is about the process. Leadership isn't a place you arrive at; it is a process you engage in, and that takes place over a long period of time. Even a lifetime.

It doesn't happen just by reading a book, going to a class, or attending a seminar. We have to continue learning, growing, applying, adjusting and re-adjusting, and many are not willing to take the journey.

There is nothing simple about leadership except its definition: leadership is influence, nothing more, nothing less. Beyond that it gets pretty complicated. It involves earning respect, gaining influence, developing emotional strength, learning people skills, becoming disciplined, learning to cast vision, delegating effectively — the list goes on. That's why leaders require so much seasoning to be truly good leaders.
So if you are going to be a great leader you need what I call the X factor: exposure and experience. These only come with time.
Two warnings
To you young aspiring leaders out there — don't rush the process. Leadership is a journey, not a destination.

To you more seasoned leaders — don't deceive yourselves into thinking you've arrived. We all have room to grow. In fact the greatest gap that exists today is the gap between what we know and what we do. So stay engaged in the process.
Success is found in your daily agenda

What am I doing every day that helps me grow in my quest to be a better leader? Ask yourself: what should I stop doing? In other words, what am I doing every day that I don't need to do, or shouldn't be doing?
